dimensions.assessment: Affects individuals seeking to qualify as accredited investors through an examination, as well as the SEC and registered national securities associations administering the test.
dimensions.evidence: allows an individual to qualify through an examination established by the Securities and Exchange Commission.

dimensions.assessment: Provides an alternative route to accredited investor status for individuals with financial sophistication, which can change their investment eligibility.
dimensions.evidence: include any natural person who is certified through the examination required under subsection (b).

dimensions.assessment: The exam must be offered free of charge to the public, but the source does not detail specific spending figures or funding appropriations.
dimensions.evidence: administered and offered free of charge to the public by a registered national securities association

dimensions.assessment: Amends regulatory definitions under Regulation D and requires the SEC to establish and oversee a new certification examination program.
dimensions.evidence: The Commission shall revise the definition of accredited investor under Regulation D... to include any natural person who is certified through the examination

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a permanent regulatory change regarding accredited investor qualifications with ongoing nationwide applicability.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than 1 year after the date of the enactment of this Act, the Commission shall establish an examination

missing_information: Specific cost estimates or budget allocations for establishing and administering the examination
The exact content or passing score requirements of the examination
importance_detail.rationale: This bill directs the SEC to create a certification examination allowing additional individuals to qualify as accredited investors for private securities offerings. While it creates a new federal credentialing pathway, the overall scope is limited to securities regulations and investor definitions without broad economy-wide fiscal outlays.
